questions.prompt: Find the real x values for which (x−1)(x−4)>0. State whether the endpoints are included. [3 marks]
markPoints: The product equals zero when x=1 or x=4.
The factors have the same sign to the left of 1 and to the right of 4.
Hence x<1 or x>4; neither endpoint is included because the inequality is strict.
questions.modelAnswer: The product equals zero when x=1 or x=4. The factors have the same sign to the left of 1 and to the right of 4. Hence x<1 or x>4; neither endpoint is included because the inequality is strict.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 2 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Given that ∫₀⁶f(x)dx=12 and ∫₂⁶f(x)dx=−5, find ∫₀²f(x)dx and justify the step. [3 marks]
markPoints: Therefore ∫₀²f(x)dx=17, even though the second given signed integral is negative.
questions.modelAnswer: By additivity, ∫₀⁶f(x)dx=∫₀²f(x)dx+∫₂⁶f(x)dx. So 12=∫₀²f(x)dx−5. Therefore ∫₀²f(x)dx=17, even though the second given signed integral is negative.

questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 2 source-linked method
questions.prompt: The circle (x−3)²+(y+2)²=49 cuts the vertical line x=3 at A and B. Find its centre, radius and both intersection coordinates. [3 marks]
markPoints: At x=3, (y+2)²=49, so the intersections are (3,5) and (3,−9).
questions.modelAnswer: Compare with (x−a)²+(y−b)²=r² to get centre (3,−2). Since r²=49, the radius is 7. At x=3, (y+2)²=49, so the intersections are (3,5) and (3,−9).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 2 source-linked method
questions.prompt: For y=x²/2+3√x, x>0, explain why the curve has no stationary points and find its tangent at x=4. [5 marks]
markPoints: For x>0 both terms are positive, so dy/dx cannot be zero and no stationary points exist.
questions.modelAnswer: Differentiate to obtain dy/dx=x+3/(2√x). For x>0 both terms are positive, so dy/dx cannot be zero and no stationary points exist. At x=4, y=8+6=14. The tangent gradient is 4+3/4=19/4. Therefore the tangent is y−14=(19/4)(x−4).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 2 source-linked method
questions.prompt: An athlete completes 12 laps on the first training day and five more laps each subsequent day. Find the first day with at least 107 laps and the total laps completed up to that day. [5 marks]
markPoints: Hence n≥20 and the first day meeting the target is day 20.
questions.modelAnswer: The nth term is uₙ=12+5(n−1)=5n+7. The target inequality is 5n+7≥107. Hence n≥20 and the first day meeting the target is day 20. The sum is S₂₀=(20/2)(2×12+19×5). Therefore S₂₀=10×119=1190 laps.

questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 2 source-linked method
questions.prompt: For an exponential model P=a bᵗ, a straight-line plot satisfies log₁₀P=0.08t+2.1. Find a and b, the percentage increase per time unit, the prediction at t=5 and one modelling limitation. [5 marks]
markPoints: Taking logs of P=a bᵗ gives log₁₀P=log₁₀a+t log₁₀b.
The prediction assumes exponential growth continues and may be unreliable far beyond the observed data.
questions.modelAnswer: Taking logs of P=a bᵗ gives log₁₀P=log₁₀a+t log₁₀b. Thus a=10^2.1≈125.9 and b=10^0.08≈1.2023. The percentage increase is 100(b−1)≈20.2%. At t=5, log₁₀P=2.5, so P=10^2.5≈316.2. The prediction assumes exponential growth continues and may be unreliable far beyond the observed data.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 2 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Let f(x)=√(9−x) for x≤9 and g(x)=2/x for x≠0. Find h(x)=g(f(x)), its maximal real domain, an inverse h⁻¹ and the domain of that inverse. [5 marks]
markPoints: The square root must be real and its value nonzero, so the maximal domain is x<9.
The range of h is y>0, so the inverse has domain x>0.
questions.modelAnswer: Composition gives h(x)=2/√(9−x). The square root must be real and its value nonzero, so the maximal domain is x<9. Write y=2/√(9−x) and rearrange to 9−x=4/y². Therefore h⁻¹(x)=9−4/x². The range of h is y>0, so the inverse has domain x>0.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 2 source-linked method
questions.prompt: For cosθ≠0, show that 1/(1−sinθ)+1/(1+sinθ)=2sec²θ. If the expression equals 8 and θ is obtuse, find tanθ exactly. [5 marks]
markPoints: Setting the expression to 8 gives sec²θ=4, hence cos²θ=1/4.
Since θ is obtuse, cosθ=−1/2 and sinθ=√3/2.
questions.modelAnswer: Combining the two fractions gives 2/(1−sin²θ). Use 1−sin²θ=cos²θ to obtain 2/cos²θ=2sec²θ. Setting the expression to 8 gives sec²θ=4, hence cos²θ=1/4. Since θ is obtuse, cosθ=−1/2 and sinθ=√3/2. Thus tanθ=sinθ/cosθ=−√3.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 2 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Find the first three terms of (1−3x)^−1/2, state the interval of validity and use the expansion to approximate the value at x=1/12. [5 marks]
markPoints: The constant and x terms are 1+(3/2)x.
questions.modelAnswer: Use (1+u)ⁿ=1+nu+n(n−1)u²/2+⋯ with n=−1/2 and u=−3x. The constant and x terms are 1+(3/2)x. The x² term is [(−1/2)(−3/2)/2]×9x²=(27/8)x². Convergence requires |−3x|<1, so −1/3<x<1/3. At x=1/12, the approximation is 1+1/8+3/128=147/128≈1.14844.

questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 2 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Prove by contradiction that x+4/x≥4 for every positive real number x. State when equality holds. [4 marks]
markPoints: Assume some positive x satisfies x+4/x<4.
Rearrange to (x−2)²<0, which is impossible for real x.
Therefore x+4/x≥4 for all x>0; equality occurs when x=2.
questions.modelAnswer: Assume some positive x satisfies x+4/x<4. Multiplying by x>0 gives x²+4<4x. Rearrange to (x−2)²<0, which is impossible for real x. Therefore x+4/x≥4 for all x>0; equality occurs when x=2.
